note.explanation: Density tells us how much mass is packed into a certain volume. Find it by dividing mass by volume.
examples: A mass of 90 g in a volume of 10 cm³ has density 90 g ÷ 10 cm³ = 9 g cm⁻³.
If a solid raises water from 40 cm³ to 44 cm³, its volume is 4 cm³.
note.simple: Density is a way of comparing how much matter is packed into the same amount of space.
note.checkQuestion: What is the density of a 30 g object with a volume of 10 cm³?
note.title: Finding density
steps: Find the mass of the substance.
Divide mass by volume: Density = Mass/Volume.
Write the answer with an appropriate density unit.

mcqs.stem: What is the density of a substance?
rationales: Correct: density is defined as mass per unit volume.
This reverses the mass and volume in the definition.
Density is found by division, not multiplication.
Weight per unit area describes pressure, not density.

mcqs.stem: Which is the SI unit of density?
rationales: Correct: the SI unit is kilograms per cubic metre.
This is mass per area, not mass per volume.
This is the unit of pressure.
This is volume per mass, the inverse of density.

mcqs.stem: A solid has a mass of 36 g and a volume of 3 cm³. What is its density?
rationales: Correct: 36 g ÷ 3 cm³ = 12 g cm⁻³.
This does not result from dividing the mass by the volume.
This multiplies the mass by the volume instead of dividing.
This reverses the mass and volume.

mcqs.stem: The water level in a measuring cylinder rises from 40 cm³ to 44 cm³ when a solid is added. What is the solid's volume?
rationales: Correct: the solid's volume is the rise in level, 44 − 40 = 4 cm³.
This is the initial water level, not the rise.
This is the final water level, not the solid's volume.
This adds the two readings instead of finding their difference.

mcqs.stem: The density of water is 1000 kg m⁻³. How is this value written in scientific notation?
rationales: This is 100, not 1000.
This is 10 000, not 1000.
This is 0.001, not 1000.

options: The one with the greater mass for the same volume
The one with the smaller mass for the same volume
The one with the larger volume for the same mass
The one with the lower temperature
mcqs.stem: Two substances have equal volumes. Which one has the greater density?
rationales: Correct: for equal volumes, the greater mass means greater mass per unit volume.
A smaller mass for the same volume means a smaller density.
For the same mass, a larger volume means a smaller density.
Temperature alone does not identify which substance has greater density.

mcqs.stem: An iron block has a mass of 94 g and a volume of 12 cm³. Which is its density to two significant figures?
rationales: Correct: 94 ÷ 12 is about 7.8 g cm⁻³.
This is ten times smaller than the quotient.
This is ten times larger than the quotient.
This uses an unsuitable unit and is not the calculated value.

options: The liquid with greater density forms the lower layer
The liquid with greater density forms the upper layer
Both liquids always mix into one layer
The liquid with lower density forms the lower layer
mcqs.stem: When immiscible liquids of different densities are mixed, which statement describes their layers?
rationales: Correct: the denser liquid settles below the less dense liquid.
The less dense liquid, not the denser one, is above.
Immiscible liquids do not mix into one layer.
The lower layer is the denser liquid, not the less dense one.

written.text: The length, breath and thickness of an iron block are 3 cm, 2 cm, 2 cm respectively. Calculate the density of iron if the mass of block is 94 g.
written.finalAnswer: Density of iron = 7800 kg m⁻³ (or 7.8 g cm⁻³).

explain.title: What density means
explain.body: Density of a substance is defined as its mass per unit volume. This means density compares the mass of a substance with the space it occupies.

explain.title: The formula and units
explain.body: Density = Mass/Volume. The SI unit of density is kg m⁻³. Another unit in use is g cm⁻³. Keep the mass and volume units consistent when calculating.

explain.title: Finding the volume of a solid
explain.body: For a regular solid, measure its dimensions and calculate its volume. For an irregular solid, place it in a liquid in a measuring cylinder; the rise in the liquid level gives the volume of the solid.

explain.title: Why substances have different densities
explain.body: Equal volumes of different substances can have different masses. Their molecules differ in size and mass, and their intermolecular spacing differs. A substance with more closely packed and heavier molecules has more mass in the same volume.

mistakes: Dividing volume by mass instead of using Density = Mass/Volume.
Using the measuring cylinder's final reading as the solid's volume instead of subtracting the initial reading.
Mixing grams with cubic metres or kilograms with cubic centimetres without converting units.
Writing a mass or volume unit instead of a density unit such as kg m⁻³ or g cm⁻³.
Leaving out the final answer or its unit after showing the calculation.
